For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Vikash Kumar, Adv.
 PRESENT  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed with a prayer for quashing the entire criminal proceedings , including the First Information Report of Sidhgora P.S. case no. 97 of 2019 involving the offences punishable under Sections 323, 313, 376, 420, 504, and 34 of Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2- victim jointly submit that they do not know whether the investigation of the case is over or whether the charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that I.A. No. 4191 of 2024 is a joint compromise petition and therein it has been mentioned that the petitioner and the opposite party no. 2 have amicably settled their dispute.

It is further submitted that the petitioner falsely obtained the consent Durga Charan Pramanik vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14510714/
1 of the opposite party no. 2 by suppressing his caste and deceiving the opposite party no. 2 that the petitioner belongs to her caste.

sentences.text: There is specific allegation that the petitioner forcibly committed rape upon the opposite party no. 2 but subsequently, promised to marry her and thereafter, the opposite party no. 2 became pregnant and the petitioner caused her miscarriage without her consent under threat.

It is next submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner and the opposite party no. 2 are happily and peacefully living their life as husband and wife, hence, it is submitted that the entire criminal proceedings of the First Information Report vide Sidhgora P.S.
case no. 97 of 2019 be quashed and set aside.

5. Learned Addl. PP on the other hand opposes the prayer for quashing and setting aside the entire criminal proceedings of the First Information Report vide Sidhgora P.S. case no. 97 of 2019 and submits that it is a settled principle of law that the offence under Seciton 376 of IPC is a heinous offence and crime against the society and the offence of such serious nature, ought not be quashed,
even if there is compromise between the parties, hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition, being without any merit be dismissed.

6. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme court of India in the case of Narinder Singh and Others vs. State of Punjab &
Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466, in paragraph 29.3, of which, reads as under:
"29.

Narinder Singh and Others vs. State of Punjab &
Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid discussion, we sum up and lay down the following principles by which the High Court would be guided in giving adequate treatment to the settlement between the parties and exercising its power under Section 482 of the Code while accepting the settlement and quashing the proceedings or refusing to accept the settlement with direction to continue with the criminal proceedings:
Xxxxxxxxxx 29.3.

Such a power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder,
rape, dacoity, etc.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, for the offences alleged to have been committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender."
(Emphasis supplied)

that the power to pass the criminal proceedings in exercise of power under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the basis of settlement, is not to be exercised in the cases, involving inter alia the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

Hence, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, and as there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner of commission of rape upon the opp.
party no. 2, the claim of subsequently leading conjugal life, certainly, will not condone the offence of rape.

Under such circumstances, this Court is not inclined to quash and set aside entire criminal proceedings of the First Information Report vide Sidhgora P.S. case no. 97 of 2019, involving serious and heinous offences involving mental depravity like the offence punishable under section 376 and 313 of the Indian Durga Charan Pramanik vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14510714/
2 Penal Code.
7.
